clock_policy.notes: The pod cannot set a clock lock and never could; the datacenter-card policy is the natural clock in any case (docs/perf/README.md section 5). Verified by observation: a step whose busy samples, those free of power, thermal and slowdown limits, never reach the card's maximum SM clock is flagged in the manifest. FSO_BENCH_WARM_MS=300 settles the clock before every timed cell.

notes: Filled on 2026-10-01 from the pod itself (pip list of the interpreter, nvidia-smi).

The card is selected by index 0, the pod's only GPU, and checked by name: its UUID and PCI id change whenever the pod is rescheduled (06:00.0 and 66:00.0 on earlier days, 16:00.0 on 2026-10-01 evening). The harness pins CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the UUID it finds and records UUID and PCI id in the manifest.

Compute mode: DEFAULT for the run and the mode found before the run restored after it, as /data/bench-runs/fso_release_perf_20261001/b300/run_stage1.sh did (it found Exclusive_Process); when the card is already in Default mode the restore is a no-op.

The PYTHONPATH overlay holds only expecttest 0.3.0 (pip install --no-deps --target): env0520 lacks it, and torch.testing._internal imports it for the reference MXFP8 quantize of the dense bench's cuBLAS columns and of the torch scaled_grouped_mm comparators. The overlay lives in the 2026-10-01 run directory; the preflight checks that expecttest resolves to 0.3.0 through it, so a moved or deleted overlay is a refusal, not a silent loss of those columns.

Package keys are distribution names: deep_gemm is the sgl-deep-gemm distribution. Every package of the harness's list that the environment has installed is pinned (sglang, deep_gemm and FlashInfer are installed but no B300 table uses them), plus nvidia-cublas, nvidia-cuda-nvrtc and the expecttest overlay.
The sm tag is 100: the B300 is sm_103, built for the 10.0f family target, and its dense baselines are named gemm_sm100_*.
